inputs.E3: FAILED — no artifacts on disk; commodities arm absent

significance_bar_inconsistency.E1_rule: paper3_E1.py:717 — significant_harvey = abs(t) > 3.0, hardcoded, no HLN correction applied at all
significance_bar_inconsistency.E2_rule: paper3_E2.py:784-791 — t = t_raw * hln_factor, then significant_harvey = abs(t) > student_t.ppf(0.975, df) ~ 1.961
significance_bar_inconsistency.consequence: the two arms publish the same field name under two different bars, so 'E1: 0 significant' and 'E2: 2 significant' are NOT comparable. Under E2's 1.96 bar, E1 would show NVDA-AMD (t=+1.974) as a copula-favoured hit and several DCC-favoured hits.
significance_bar_inconsistency.resolution: this synthesis ignores both stored flags and recomputes every p-value from (t, n_oos) on one uniform rule, then applies BH-FDR.

hln_coverage.note: E1 stores raw DM t. With n_oos > 1500 the HLN factor exceeds 0.9997, so applying it shifts E1's largest |t| (GOOGL-META/Clayton, 2.8880) only to 2.8875 — it cannot change any verdict at any bar considered here.

caveats.best_copula_selection: t_best = max(t_student_t, t_clayton) is a selected maximum; inference uses all 44 tests with BH-FDR instead.
caveats.overlapping_samples: pairs share underlying assets (esp. TW0050, SPY), so BH-FDR independence is approximate — it is the lenient direction.

D1_lambda_L_scaling.headline: the ONLY significant lambda_L relation in either source study is E2/Clayton, and its sign is POSITIVE — i.e. significantly OPPOSITE to the pre-registered H3 prediction. E1 is null. The correct statement is not 'no relation' but 'a significant relation running backwards in one study, null in the other'.

lambda_L_support.note: the two arms barely overlap in lambda_L support, so the pooled Spearman is not a pooled estimate of one within-study relation — read the per-study rows.

heterogeneity_E1_vs_E2_clayton.verdict: significant heterogeneity — a naive 22-pair pooled Spearman is NOT a defensible primary estimator; report the study-level rhos instead.

D1e_fz_family.note: FZ0 loss on VaR/ES forecasts (Patton-Ziegel), lower = better; same DCC-first sign convention as the QLIKE family, so t > 0 favours the copula.

D1f_trinity_calibration.interpretation: Copula-GARCH beats DCC on VaR/ES calibration at alpha=2.5% (Copula-t 19/22 vs DCC 10/22), but the ordering REVERSES at alpha=1% (Copula-t 18/22 vs DCC 19/22; in E1 alone, 8/12 vs 11/12). So the calibration advantage is real but NOT uniform across tail depth — it is a 2.5% phenomenon that does not survive into the deeper tail. This is a CALIBRATION claim, not a lambda_L-threshold claim: it does not rescue Paper 3 A's main argument, but the synthesis must report it so the negative finding is not overstated in the other direction.

D1d_survivor_concentration.note: TW0050 occupies the top of the ranking; E2's asia_intraregional 'cluster' is 3 mutually overlapping pairs drawn from only 3 assets (TW0050, HSI, N225), so it is closer to one observation than to three.
